text:
vikram: Heads up — ran into quota attribution weirdness when a service-account key from Org-B is used by an app in Project-A behind our proxy. Requests billed to Project-A but quota/usage counted on Org-B. Anyone else seen this?

sara: Can you paste a minimal repro (headers + example request/response)?

vikram: Sure, here's sanitized curl we used:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sa_XXXX\" \
  -H \"X-Project-Id: project-a\" \
  -H \"X-Org-Id: org-b\" \
  -d '{\"model\":\"gptx\",\"input\":\"hi\"}'
```

Response headers include `X-Quota-Owner: org-b` but billing shows tokens on project-a. Logs show `auth.decoded_owner=org-b` and `request.presenting_project=project-a`. :thinking:

noah: This is expected from current design: we attach both `owner` (from key) and `presenting_project` (from route/metadata). Our quota enforcement was keyed off `owner` for historical reasons. That causes the mismatch when frontends forward a project header.

ashley: Problem is UX & billing surprise. Many customers expect quotas to follow where the request originated (presenting project), not the key owner. We should decide default for attribution and provide a clear migration plan. :eyes: 

noah: Agreed. Two options: 1) keep `owner` as quota key (safer, enforces key-level limits), or 2) switch to `effective_project` derived from presenting_project if present, else owner (more intuitive for multi-tenant setups).

vikram: If we change to presenting_project by default, risk is that a malicious frontend could spoof headers to escape quotas. But we already authenticate the header by verifying the proxy identity in our routing policy, right?

noah: We verify proxy identity for dedicated/private, but some customers run custom proxies that aren't fully attested. So we need a guard: only accept `presenting_project` if the upstream cert/assertion is trusted (we have `route.trust_level`).

infra-bot: deploy: auth-service v2.14.0 rolled to staging at 1769990050 (canary=5%).

ashley: Console needs to show both fields side-by-side on request detail and in Usage UI ("Auth key owner" vs "Effective attribution"). That'll reduce billing disputes during migration. Also add a notice in billing CSVs with both columns.

vikram: For telemetry, we should emit `attribution.mode` (`owner`|`presenting_project`|`hybrid`) and `attribution.mismatch=true` when owner != effective. Also a counter `auth.attribution_mismatch_total` tagged by org and presenting_project.

noah: +1. And rate-limit evaluation should run against the `effective` entity once we flip the toggle, but keep `owner` as fallback.

ashley: UX proposal: rollout as follows:
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): telemetry-only, add UI columns, add admin warning banner.
- Phase 2 (canary 10%): introduce config flag `auth.attribution_mode=effective` per route/org. Quotas still enforced on owner unless flag set.
- Phase 3 (90 days): if no regressions, flip default to `effective` and keep both columns in UI for 6 months.

vikram: Sounds reasonable. Need to document the security gate: only routes with `route.trust_level >= attested` can set presenting_project as authoritative. Fallback to owner if not attested.

noah: Implementation notes:
- auth-service: compute `effective_id = if (presenting_project && route.trust) presenting_project else owner`
- emit `auth.effective_id` and `auth.owner_id` in logs and trace attributes
- quota service: add config `quota.attribution_source` (owner|effective) and support per-tenant override

ashley: Assignments:
- noah -> implement auth-service attr logic + telemetry (ETA 1 week)
- vikram -> add request-level logging + unit tests + integration with proxy attestation (ETA 1 week)
- sara -> billing UI columns + admin banner + update docs (ETA 2 weeks)

noah: One more thing — we should add a quick `attribution_preview` endpoint on console so org admins can paste a key + sample headers and see how requests would be attributed under current vs new mode. Low effort, high signal.

ashley: Love it. Add `attribution_preview` to phase 1.

vikram: I'll also add a tiny canary smoke: generate 100 requests with presenting_project spoof and verify counters to detect spoofing.

sara: Documenting decisions in RFC doc (link placeholder) and will post a summary to #announcements before phase 2. :+1:

noah: Okay, creating tickets now. We'll track rollout on eng-board and set up alerts for `auth.attribution_mismatch_total` spikes.

ashley: Thanks all — this should reduce billing confusion and keep abuse surface controlled. :rocket:
